claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr constitute a set of low-activation refractory elements.
The initial WTaTiVZr alloy has a refined grain structure.
The initial WTaTiVZr alloy contains a mixture of BCC and FCC phases.
Under high-temperature mechanical loading, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten.
Under high-temperature mechanical loading, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercially used pure tungsten.
A stable, refined grain structure contributes to the enhanced plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr.
Activation of multiple slip systems contributes to the enhanced plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr.
The chemical composition and resulting lattice distortion facilitate formation or stability of the refined grain structure.
The chemical composition and resulting lattice distortion facilitate activation of multiple slip systems.
Grain boundaries and dislocation networks accommodate plastic strain and facilitate slip transfer.
More efficient strain accommodation and slip transfer increase plastic strain and toughness.
WTaTiVZr is predicted to show a 20% increase in plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr is predicted to show a 30% increase in toughness relative to pure tungsten.
The commercial pure-tungsten baseline has a grain size of 10 micrometers.
The commercial pure-tungsten baseline has a yield strength of 500 MPa.
The predicted performance is applicable from 800 to 1200 degrees Celsius at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
Outside the stated temperature and strain-rate range, the alloy may not exhibit the predicted behavior.
The proposed service condition lasts 100 hours at a plasma flux of 10^22 ions/m^2s.
The hypothesis is falsified if both the plastic-strain increase is below 10% and the toughness increase is below 20% relative to pure tungsten.
